nodes.label: Live worktree following via filesystem events
nodes.rationale: Driven by filesystem events rather than a polling timer so an idle repository costs nothing and a busy one coalesces into a single refresh instead of a hundred.

nodes.label: Project discovery from herdr pane working directories
nodes.rationale: Projects are derived from the working directories of herdr's open panes rather than a configured list; several panes in one repository collapse into one entry so the same repo is never shown twice.

nodes.label: Workspace scope toggle
nodes.rationale: Opens scoped to the current workspace to avoid overwhelming the pane, with `w` widening to every repository herdr has open, each as its own foldable subtree.

nodes.label: Inline diff viewer
nodes.rationale: Puts the diff where the user is already looking so reading a change costs no context switch; a position indicator orients the reader inside a long diff.

nodes.label: Diff scope: working tree vs HEAD
nodes.rationale: Staged, unstaged and untracked changes are unified into one tree compared against HEAD, so the user sees everything that strayed regardless of index state.

nodes.label: Claude agent hand-off
nodes.rationale: The prompt is typed into the target repository's agent input with the file path attached but deliberately not submitted, so the user reviews the text and presses Enter themselves.

nodes.label: Safe editor launch ($VISUAL then $EDITOR)
nodes.rationale: The file path is passed as its own argv entry behind a `--` separator and never reaches a shell, so a hostile filename from someone else's branch stays a filename instead of becoming a command.

nodes.label: Read-only git invariant
nodes.rationale: Every git call is a query: no add, commit, checkout or stash, and nothing is written to refs/, so the plugin can never damage the user's worktree or history.

nodes.label: Glyph status markers (M A D ? R S)
nodes.rationale: Meaning is carried by the glyph rather than by colour so mono terminals and colour-blind readers lose no information.

nodes.label: Show-all-tracked-files view
nodes.rationale: Unchanged files join the list dimmed so a change stands out against the surrounding repository rather than floating without context.

nodes.label: Honours .gitignore
nodes.rationale: Ignored build output must never reach the tree, otherwise generated files drown the real changes.

nodes.label: Large-directory auto-folding threshold (25 strays)
nodes.rationale: A directory holding 25 or more strays starts folded with its count shown, so a generated-output tree cannot bury real work.

nodes.label: Submodule handling
nodes.rationale: Submodules are shown as `S` but never offered to an editor because a gitlink is a directory, not a file.

nodes.label: Branch display with detached-HEAD fallback
nodes.rationale: A detached HEAD shows its short commit rather than the useless word `HEAD`, so the user can still identify where the repo sits.

nodes.label: Plugin install and key binding configuration
nodes.rationale: Install builds from source (requires a Rust toolchain); `plugin link` from a checkout skips the build step, so `cargo build --release` must be run first.

nodes.label: aleslanger.strays.open plugin action
nodes.rationale: Pressing the bound key again focuses the existing pane instead of opening a second one, and pressing it while focused dismisses the pane — a single-instance toggle.

nodes.label: CI workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs on pushes to master and on every pull request; CARGO_TERM_COLOR=always keeps cargo output readable in the Actions log.

nodes.label: check job (fmt, clippy, test)
nodes.rationale: Gates on cargo fmt --check, clippy with -D warnings across all targets, and cargo test.

nodes.label: ubuntu/macos OS matrix
nodes.rationale: The integration tests shell out to the real git binary and the plugin only claims linux and macos, so both platforms are worth running; fail-fast is disabled so one platform's failure does not hide the other's.

nodes.label: Give git an identity step
nodes.rationale: The integration tests create commits, so a global git user.name/user.email must exist even where the test helper does not set one.

nodes.label: audit job (rustsec/audit-check)
nodes.rationale: audit-check publishes findings as a check run, which the default read-only token cannot create, so checks: write is granted explicitly. It fails on vulnerabilities while unmaintained/unsound advisories are reported without blocking; the classification lives in .cargo/audit.toml so CI and `make audit` agree.

nodes.label: Shared advisory policy in .cargo/audit.toml
nodes.rationale: Severity classification is kept in .cargo/audit.toml rather than in workflow flags so the CI run and a local `make audit` produce the same verdict — one source of truth avoids drift between local and CI gates.
